newsitem.title: GERMANY: Residents win new hearing on German nuclear dump.
newsitem.headline: Residents win new hearing on German nuclear dump.

text.p: Neighbours of Germany's Morsleben nuclear waste dump won a new hearing for their safety fears on Wednesday.
The Berlin high administrative court ruled that a lower court in Magdeburg had not examined properly the worries of local residents.
The Morsleben dump was set up in East Germany in communist times and has continued in use since unification. It is the only site in Germany used for permanent disposal of nuclear waste.

Opponents, supported by Greenpeace environmental group, want waste shipments to the dump halted. They argue that water could seep into the facility 500 metres (1,600 feet) below the surface and cause the ground to cave in.
The German government says the dump is safe but announced this month that it was dropping plans to expand Morsleben and said new shipments would stop by the year 2003.
Bonn will now focus its waste disposal plans on dumps at Gorleben and Schacht Konrad in northern Germany.
